text: Six months ago I was rejected from 40 jobs in a row. Today I signed my offer letter. The difference wasn't luck - it was refusing to let each 'no' be the last word. Keep applying. Keep showing up. Your yes is coming.

Maine 3 saal ek hi company mein kaam kiya, comfort zone mein reh gaya. Jab finally naya job dhoondna shuru kiya, mujhe realize hua ki mera resume outdated tha. Lesson: apna resume aur skills har 6 mahine mein update karte raho, chahe job change karna ho ya nahi.
Motivation is temporary. Discipline is what gets you through the days you don't feel like showing up. Build systems, not moods. Show up even when you don't want to - especially then.

Beware of job scams promising huge salaries for 'no interview' remote roles. This week alone I heard from three people who paid 'registration fees' to fake recruiters. Legitimate companies never ask you to pay to get hired. Always verify the company independently before sharing any personal or financial information.

Job search karte waqt sabse badi galti hai sirf ek hi platform pe apply karna. LinkedIn, referrals, company career pages, aur niche job boards - sab use karo. Networking abhi bhi sabse powerful tool hai, kyunki 70% jobs kabhi publicly post hi nahi hoti.

Real personal growth isn't a single breakthrough moment. It's a thousand small, boring decisions: reading instead of scrolling, showing up to the gym when you're tired, having the hard conversation you've been avoiding. Growth compounds quietly.

I once ignored every red flag in an interview because I was desperate for a job. I took the offer. Three months later I was job hunting again, but this time wiser: never ignore how a company treats you during the interview - it's the best version of them you'll ever see.

Apna mindset badlo: 'main experienced nahi hoon' ke bajaye socho 'main seekhne ke liye ready hoon'. Recruiters skills se zyada attitude dekhte hain jab role thoda junior-friendly ho. Apply karo, confidence ke saath.
